skills.name: about-me
skills.description: Use when someone asks what this skill pack is, who built or maintains it, or how it compares to another agent-skill framework -- introduce the author alongside the actual answer, not for ordinary technical or architecture tasks.

skills.name: agent-development-process
skills.description: Use when building or improving an AI-agent product whose task contract, autonomy, tools, context, memory, orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, release, or operations must be designed.

skills.name: application-client-server-architecture
skills.description: Use when an application crosses client/server, API, persistence, identity, transaction, state-authority, data-history, deployment, or operational boundaries.

skills.name: architecture-review
skills.description: Use when comparing or assessing architecture decisions, module boundaries, state ownership, distributed design, platform/domain separation, failure behavior, or migration risk.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Use when production C, C++, C#, Qt, WinForms, WPF, framework, device-control, communication, or industrial code must be checked for correctness, concurrency, state, lifetime, recovery, maintainability, or boundary violations.

skills.name: codebase-architecture-discovery
skills.description: Use when a codebase area is being extended, is unfamiliar, or is suspected of accumulated duplication, and no current architecture map or duplication survey exists for it -- before proposing or executing any specific refactor.

skills.name: coding-agent-git-discipline
skills.description: Use when a coding agent must commit, push, branch, or clean up git state safely -- avoiding shell-quoting bugs in commit messages, verifying an existing PR's real branch name before pushing fixes, recovering from a failed GitHub push without a login loop, detecting a possibly-shared working tree before committing, and reminding about an overdue version/release cut.

skills.name: coding-agent-project-governance
skills.description: Use when a repository needs coding-agent instructions, risk routing, worktree rules, multi-agent ownership, test evidence, migration controls, release rules, or truthful handoff.

skills.name: cross-platform-native-architecture
skills.description: Use when a native or Qt system spans OS-specific lifecycle, HID/USB devices, firmware update, privileged integration, packaging, Designer plug-ins, or Qt build/version migration boundaries.

skills.name: development-process-tailoring
skills.description: Use when delivery is constrained by unstable requirements, hardware dependencies, release trains, urgent work, field feedback, product variants, stage gates, or competing lifecycle models.

skills.name: document-governance
skills.description: Use when engineering documents disagree on authority, version lineage, audience, approval state, traceability, terminology, source data, or release baseline.

skills.name: equipment-control-architecture
skills.description: Use when equipment software coordinates material flow, pump/vent or chamber readiness, wafer/lot sequences, robots, recipes, interlocks, shared physical resources, simulation, or distributed control across equipment modules.

skills.name: equipment-domain-modeling
skills.description: Use when modeling valves, MFCs, pumps, gauges, heaters, power supplies, robots, chamber snapshots, equipment commands, hardware readback, Actual and Desired values, capabilities, engineering units, or metadata-driven UI.

skills.name: framework-design
skills.description: Use when reusable capability must be separated from product or domain behavior through framework, SDK, plug-in, platform, extension-point, state/command, or product-line contracts.

skills.name: project-management-sync
skills.description: Use when safely auditing, previewing, reconciling, or applying synchronization of plans, tasks, statuses, dates, or project records between a local or internal backlog and external project-management systems such as Vikunja, OpenProject, or Redmine, especially when provider versions/capabilities may drift, duplicate writes must be prevented, credentials must work across macOS/Windows/Ubuntu/CI, or every mutation needs post-write verification.

skills.name: safe-incremental-refactoring
skills.description: Use when legacy or brownfield responsibilities must move without breaking behavior, public contracts, data, transaction order, release compatibility, recovery, or test seams.

skills.name: semiconductor-equipment-domain-knowledge
skills.description: Use when a semiconductor-equipment task depends on the physical meaning of EFEM, load ports, loadlocks, transfer chambers, process chambers, vacuum pumps, pressure gauges, gas flow, heaters, power supplies, plasma, sputtering, or process readiness.

skills.name: software-quality-iso25010
skills.description: Use when software quality must be translated into measurable scenarios, acceptance criteria, metrics, evidence, dashboards, release gates, or defect analysis using ISO/IEC 25010.

skills.name: teach-while-building
skills.description: Use when the user wants to build mastery of relevant knowledge as a side effect of real engineering work, not as a separate course — a new concept, quirk, or non-obvious constraint surfaces mid-task and its durable understanding is worth checking.

skills.name: using-cloudbox-skills
skills.description: Use when a non-trivial engineering task may require one or more CloudBox skills, especially when it refers to prior corrections or interactions, spans architecture, equipment, code, process, quality, documents, or AI agents, or has ambiguous routing and skill composition.
